clue.text: Instrument — one of several children brought to rave

parts.note: a quad is a quadruplet, one of four children born together
to rave is to rant

explanation.surface: A musical instrument given to one of a family's many children so they can make a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests music, but a quadrant is an angle-measuring navigational instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrant is an old navigational tool for measuring the altitude of stars, so it counts as an instrument.

clue.text: Source of stone is what one seeks …

definitions.meaning: a pit where stone is dug out

explanation.definitionFit: A quarry is both a stone pit and the prey a hunter pursues.

clue.text: … seeker after stone St Michael confounded

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A searcher for a certain stone baffled St Michael.
explanation.walkthrough: The stone is the philosopher's stone, carried over from 1 down by the ellipsis; 'confounded' mixes STMICHAEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Alchemists sought the philosopher's stone, which was meant to turn base metal into gold.

clue.text: List featuring old Chanticleer

indicators.note: featuring means the list holds the letter for old within it

parts.note: a roster is a list of names

explanation.surface: A list of characters includes the old cockerel from the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Chanticleer is the cockerel in Chaucer's Nun's Priest's Tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Chanticleer is the traditional name for a cockerel in fable, a male farmyard bird.

clue.text: No way you can see inside grave

indicators.note: inside means the way goes within the word for no

parts.note: nay means no
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Nobody can look inside a tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' reads as a tomb but is the adjective meaning serious; 'you can see' is link padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A nasty injury is a grave or serious one, so the adjectives are synonyms here.

clue.text: The highest point of a river attracting expression of surprise

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river, a crossword favourite
gee is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone gasps on reaching the top of a river's course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attracting' simply has the river draw the exclamation along after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The apogee is the culmination or peak of something, originally the furthest point of an orbit from Earth.

clue.text: In the afternoon, Dickens' hero meets eponymous heroine

parts.note: Pip is the hero of Dickens's Great Expectations
Emma is the title heroine of Jane Austen's novel Emma

explanation.surface: An afternoon meeting between characters from two classic novels.
explanation.walkthrough: Pip emma is old British military signallers' slang for p.m.
explanation.definitionFit: Signallers' alphabet spelt PM as pip emma, so the phrase is old slang for afternoon.

clue.text: Vigorous enjoyment got us in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters are in disarray and rearranged

explanation.surface: Excessive high spirits landed us in a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty relish or zest in doing something.

clue.text: English chap on island heading north for port

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Ron is a typical chap's name
isle means island

explanation.surface: An Englishman on an island sails north to a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'on' means above, and 'heading north' turns the whole run upwards. Elsinore, the Danish port of Helsingor, is the setting of Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsinore (Helsingor) is a Danish port town, the setting of Hamlet.

clue.text: Force speculator to go off

parts.note: a bull is a stock market speculator who buys expecting prices to rise
to go off to sleep is to doze

explanation.surface: A speculator is made to leave by force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' means drop off to sleep, not leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To bulldoze someone is to force or bully them into something.

clue.text: Coming upon a zebra, you may be misunderstanding each other

definitions.text: Coming upon a zebra, you may be
definitions.meaning: a zebra is a British striped pedestrian crossing, so someone arriving at one is at a crossing, here read as being at cross for one's purposes
the idiom for two parties talking past one another with different aims

explanation.surface: A driver meeting a zebra crossing finds that driver and pedestrian have got their wires crossed.
explanation.walkthrough: A zebra is a British pedestrian crossing marked with black and white stripes, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes people working with different, conflicting aims because neither understands the other.

clue.text: Never backward with experiment forming part of space shuttle mission

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the poetic form of never from end to start

parts.note: ne'er is the poetic contraction of never
a try is an attempt or experiment

explanation.surface: An astronaut who never flinches tries something new during a shuttle flight.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'It' in the held clue is the clue number II misread. NE'ER read backward gives REEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-entry, coming back into the atmosphere, is a stage of every space shuttle flight.

clue.text: Make fun of lighting — nothing's working

parts.note: a lamp provides lighting
O, the round figure zero, means nothing
on means working, as a switched-on machine is

explanation.surface: Someone complains that none of the lights in the place will come on.
explanation.definitionFit: To lampoon someone is to ridicule them publicly, usually in satire.

clue.text: Trio belt out the words

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A three-piece group bellows the lyrics of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' reshuffles TRIOBELT.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the text of an opera or musical, the words set to music.

clue.text: Note to promote not very social occasion

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: not says the letter for very is left out

parts.note: to advance someone is to promote them

explanation.surface: A memo about promotion at a not-very-social event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very' seems to qualify 'social' but removes V from ADVANCE. A tea dance is an afternoon dance with tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea dance is an afternoon dancing party with tea served, a social gathering.

clue.text: Stronger queen put on jack led originally

indicators.note: put on means the queen is placed after the other pieces

parts.note: jack is slang for a sailor, as is AB, able seaman

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of led is taken

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: In a card game, a queen laid on a jack that was led first proves the stronger card.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-game picture misleads: jack is a sailor (AB) and the queen is ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Abler is the comparative of able, so more capable or stronger.

clue.text: It's ridiculous, losing one — absurd and ridiculous

indicators.note: absurd suggests the remaining letters are arranged nonsensically
losing means one letter drops out of the word

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral, means one

explanation.surface: Something so silly it is absurd, ridiculous even.
explanation.walkthrough: RIDICULOUS less one I gives RDICULOUS, which 'absurd' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludicrous and ridiculous are synonyms, both meaning laughably absurd.

clue.text: Misshape's twisted by stress

indicators.note: twisted means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A deformed object is bent further under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's adds no letter: 'twisted' rearranges MISSHAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is stress laid on a word or point.

clue.text: Fit for the game

definitions.meaning: to fit is to suit or correspond to something
a game or contest between sides

explanation.definitionFit: To match is to fit or go with something, and a match is also a sporting game.

clue.text: Cry of praise in biblical book an unfinished record

parts.note: Hos is the abbreviation for Hosea, an Old Testament book

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: an annal is a year's record

explanation.surface: A shout of praise found in scripture, an incomplete account.
explanation.walkthrough: HOS is Hosea; ANNAL loses its final L.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosanna is a liturgical shout of praise and adoration.

clue.text: The Queen's in town

definitions.meaning: The queen consort of William IV
the capital of South Australia, named after her

explanation.surface: Gossip that Her Majesty is visiting.
explanation.walkthrough: Adelaide was queen to William IV of Britain; the Australian city was named after her.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian city bears the name of the queen consort of William IV, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Guide these days needed on a peak

parts.note: AD, anno domini, covers the present era
the peak of a cap is its visor

explanation.surface: A mountain guide is needed nowadays on a summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peak' suggests a mountain but is the brim of a cap.
explanation.definitionFit: An advisor guides others by giving counsel.

clue.text: Saint a rather unruly type, it's said

parts.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth thought somewhat rowdy

explanation.surface: Gossip that a saint was something of a tearaway.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style clothes, seen as a troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Stated and said are both past participles meaning expressed in words.

clue.text: Possible result of tossing, with each series of waves coming straight at boat

definitions.text: series of waves coming straight at boat

parts.note: tossing a coin may come down heads

explanation.surface: A sailor tossing a coin while waves pound the bows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossing' points at the sea's motion but is a coin toss.
explanation.definitionFit: A head sea is a nautical term for waves running directly against a vessel's course.

clue.text: Someone from north of the border put together this course

indicators.note: put together says the two pieces join into one word

parts.note: a, as in a person, stands for someone
a Scot comes from north of the English border

explanation.surface: A Scotsman assembled this racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: A SCOT run together is Ascot, the English racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire, home of Royal Ascot.

clue.text: Do check about firm providing accommodation for fliers

indicators.note: about says the word for check goes around the firm

parts.note: to vet is to check or examine
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: An instruction to inspect a company that provides housing for airline crews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fliers' suggests air travellers but means birds; VET goes about CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovecot is a house built for doves or pigeons to roost in.

clue.text: Aquatic bird — it's used to fish

definitions.meaning: a mayfly or artificial fly used by anglers

explanation.definitionFit: A drake is a male duck, and in angling a drake is a mayfly pattern used as bait.

clue.text: Tick form and send off — it's not vital mail

parts.note: a tick is a moment, a second
a form is a school class
to post a letter is to send it off

explanation.surface: Instructions to tick boxes on a form and then mail it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tick' and 'form' read as paperwork; a tick is a moment and a form is a school class.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-class post is the cheaper, slower British mail service used for letters that are not urgent.

clue.text: Band protecting a provincial governor

indicators.note: protecting means the band wraps around the letter it guards

parts.note: a strap is a band of leather or similar

explanation.surface: A musical group acting as bodyguard for a regional official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks musical but is a STRAP, which goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was the governor of a province in ancient Persia.

clue.text: Repeated rejection of one wanting to seize power

indicators.note: rejection, a turning back, says the whole is read backwards
to seize means the wanting one grabs and holds the power letter inside

parts.note: a desirer is someone who wants

explanation.surface: A coup leader's bid for power is turned down once again.
explanation.walkthrough: DESIRER seizes P to make DESIRPER, which 'rejection of' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprise is to repeat a song or role, so reprised means repeated.
